decision: WHICH STACK IS LIVE, on pristine vsavj. A probe copy of walker_sp.lua (walker_sp_probe.lua) ran the ghost audit's own legs (probe.sh). Its diff only ADDS reads of SR, SP, USP, the long at each, and the frames each site fires on (the frames were added after the vanilla run; aggregate.log does not use them). The legs: every legacy replay with a vanilla basis log (56), at sites 0x54476 and 0x5E548. From aggregate.log:
- The S bit is clear on all 8,586 and all 315,008 hits.
- walker_sp.lua's own read (A7 or SP) is 0xFF7FF6, the supervisor stack, which is walker_ghost.toml's frozen sp_min = sp_max = 0xff7ff6.
- USP reads 0xFF06DE at the first site and 0xFF055E..0xFF06DE at the second.
Ground truth (ground_truth.log, the vsavj opcode image): the long at USP is the return of a `jsr abs.l` to a walker, ending exactly on it, on 323,594 of 323,594 hits. The long at SP is, on 0 of them.

ON THE SHIPPED BUILD. probe_m20.sh ran the legacy oracle's own 53 replays on merged-m20 (build/m3b_merged28), where the relocation is live (relocation_m20.log: the ten walker call sites the corpus reaches jump to the copies 0x4C1400 / 0x4C1290). From windows_m20.log:
- The vanilla sites fire 0 times.
- The relocated `jsr (A0)` sites (0x4C12AE, 0x4C141E, disassembled in relocated_sites_dis.txt) run in USER mode on all 8,591 and 289,903 hits, with USP 0xFF06DE and 0xFF055E..0xFF06DE, as on vanilla.
So the relocated push, at USP-4..USP-1, lands within $FF055A-$FF06DD, outside $FF7F00-$FF7FFF. walker_ghost's premise does not hold, and its PASS measured the idle stack.

WHAT THE ORACLE DOES AND DOES NOT SHOW. Its mask (oracle_mask.txt) does not cover $FF055A-$FF06DD, and its checksum SEES that range. plant_ctl.sh ran the oracle's own instrument (tests/lua/replay.lua) and mask on M20, replay 01_attract_long (exact class). A byte poked at $FF06DA at frame 1200 moves the checksum from frame 1200 on. The same poke at $FF7FF2, inside the masked window, moves it on no frame (plant_ctl.log). On M20 the oracle passed 53/53, but only 2 replays are exact: 38 pass as window and 13 as composite (merged_legacy_m20base.log). windows_m20.log counts the relocated walker's frames against each replay's tolerated frames (the .masked window and composite ranges). A hit labelled N ran in the oracle's frame N+1: both walker_sp.lua and replay.lua increment their counter at the start of frame_done (walker_sp.lua:111, replay_frame_done.txt). Both alignments are counted, and they give 3 either way and 52,441 against 52,445:
- 8,588 + 237,462 walker frames lie OUTSIDE every tolerated range. There the oracle demanded identity and got it, so the pushed value was gone by those checksums.
- 3 + 52,441 lie INSIDE a tolerated range, mostly the select-screen windows. There a surviving push would pass unseen. This is UNMEASURED.
tests/audit_walker_repoint.sh uses only hit counts, so no stack value reaches its verdict.
THE RECOMMENDATION.
(1) walker_sp.lua reads `(SR & 0x2000) ~= 0 and SP or USP` (the rule of docs/platform/gotchas.md:2653-2673), with the ground-truth check in the consuming gate.
(2) audit_walker_ghost's inside-the-mask premise is retracted in its header, walker_ghost.toml and the docs. The maintainer chooses the re-statement between:
(a) freeze the live ranges and assert the push lies outside every oracle mask, the in-window frames named as uncovered;
(b) also measure the ghost slots directly inside the windows, a new instrument;
(c) retire the gate, leaving legacy safety to the oracle.
(3) Today's duplicate gotcha (docs/platform/gotchas.md:2973-2980, the #176 entry on SP and USP) is reconciled with the 14z-158 entry (lines 2653-2673).
